crime: Every evening in the dining hall, one prisoner mended the other girls' torn clothes, cutting each patch from the dress she had arrived in. A patch took her a quarter of an hour, and at half past nine she handed everything back.
{WITCH_NAME}'s mother used to unpick her name tag from each school uniform at the resale counter. "Someone else will wear it." Nothing she wore ever stayed hers.
At ten to nine, she brought the mender a torn dress for the first time. She had torn it herself. The mender handed it back unpatched. "Patches are for clothes people keep."

Just before nine, {WITCH_NAME} took the tailor's shears from the table and drove them into the mender's neck. Then she put on each of the three garments still waiting in the basket and, with her Magic, pictured it mended. Each came off patched just like the mender's work, and she folded it onto the finished pile. From nine, she sat with the other girls in the lounge until the body was found.

At half past nine, the prisoners came for their clothes and found the mender dead, every garment patched and folded, the basket empty. One girl had left her torn skirt last in the basket at a quarter to nine, with three garments still waiting. In the trial court, they concluded that the mender had been working on those three patches from a quarter to nine until just before half past nine, while {WITCH_NAME} sat in the lounge.

But the mender had shown every girl she helped the hole in her own dress where that girl's patch had been cut. One prisoner searched it for holes matching the three new patches and found none. The court saw then that the mender had never sewn those three. Someone wearing each garment had pictured its patch, and the mender had died before nine, when {WITCH_NAME} had not yet sat down in the lounge.
fields.epitaph: She knew every patch the girl had ever sewn, but never where one was cut, because none had ever been cut for her.
fields.epithet: Dressed for Every Circle, Kept by None
execution: The execution stand raises a tall, turning clothes rack hung with every outfit she ever pictured. She stands bound to its pole by the sleeves of the first. As the rack turns, the hangers drop their outfits over her head one after another. Each settles over the last, and none replaces it. The last hanger lowers a plain dress onto the top, an empty name tag at its collar. The heap of clothes stirs, then stops, the empty name tag uppermost.

magic.name: Dream Wardrobe
magic.text: She can turn whatever she's wearing into any outfit she pictures, real enough to wear.
